Objective
To be a key member of the Mission to Seafarers South Australia team, providing welfare services to visiting seafarers while supporting the sustainable development and operation of Mission to Seafarers centres across South Australia.
Based in Port Pirie, the Port Welfare Officers will share responsibility for providing seafarer welfare services, supporting volunteers and committees, coordinating administration, and assisting with the development of services in all South Australian ports, including Port Adelaide,  Port Lincoln, Port Giles, Thevenard, Wallaroo and any future centres established within the state.
The role combines practical seafarer welfare, volunteer coordination, administration, stakeholder engagement and centre development.

Level of Responsibility
The Port Welfare Officers report directly to the Regional Director, Mission to Seafarers Australia.
They work closely with the South Australian Management Committee, local port committees, volunteers, port authorities, shipping agents, churches and other stakeholders to ensure effective delivery of welfare services throughout the state.

The role shares responsibility for:
Day-to-day operation of the Port Pirie Seafarers Centre.
Development and support of Mission to Seafarers activities throughout South Australia.
Volunteer recruitment, training and support.
Administrative and financial management of the South Australian operations.
Regular travel to South Australian ports to visit ships, support volunteers and strengthen relationships with industry partners.

Conditions
The successful applicant will be required to maintain:
Current Driver's Licence.
National Police Check.
Safe Church Communities accreditation (or equivalent).
Working With Children Check (or applicable state screening requirements).
Australian Border Force and Port Security access requirements as required.
Capacity to travel throughout South Australia, including overnight travel where necessary.

About the Role
This position would suit someone who is passionate about improving the welfare of seafarers, enjoys working with volunteers and industry, is highly organised, flexible and self-motivated, and is comfortable working across multiple locations.
The role requires initiative, strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships with maritime industry stakeholders while developing sustainable welfare services across regional ports.

Knowledge and Experience
The successful applicant will possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills together with confidence using technology.
A sound working knowledge of Microsoft Office, Xero or similar accounting software, databases, social media and web-based systems is desirable.

Essential Skills and Experience
Office administration experience.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organisational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a small team.
Proficient in Microsoft Office.
Experience using accounting software (preferably Xero).
Experience coordinating volunteers or community programs.
Current driver's licence and willingness to travel.
Desirable Skills and Experience
Experience preparing agendas, minutes and financial reports.
Website and social media management.
Marketing and communications experience.
Fundraising and grant administration.
Community development experience.
Understanding of the Mission to Seafarers and the maritime industry.
Experience working with committees or not-for-profit organisations.

Duties and Responsibilities
1. Seafarer Welfare
Visit ships and provide welfare support to visiting seafarers.
Coordinate transport, shopping, communications and welfare services.
Supply SIM cards, Wi-Fi access and welfare items.
Assist with emergency welfare situations when required.
Promote compliance with the Maritime Labour Convention welfare provisions.
2. Centre and Port Development
Support the ongoing development of Mission to Seafarers services throughout South Australia.
Assist with establishing and growing welfare activities in new and developing ports.
Identify opportunities to improve facilities and services.
Build relationships with port authorities, shipping agents, terminal operators and industry stakeholders.
Promote awareness of seafarer welfare across the maritime community.
3. Administration
Prepare agendas, reports and committee meeting minutes.
Complete and maintain Australian Border Force documentation.
Maintain registrations, licences and compliance records.
Monitor donations and acknowledge supporters.
Support committee office bearers with administration.
Manage SIM cards, vouchers and foreign currency.
Assist the Regional Director with reporting and projects.
4. Communications and Marketing
Monitor incoming enquiries.
Coordinate communications with volunteers, shipping agents and port stakeholders.
Maintain websites and social media platforms.
Produce promotional material highlighting Mission activities.
Represent Mission to Seafarers at community and industry events.
5. Volunteer Management
Recruit new volunteers across South Australia.
Coordinate induction, training and mentoring.
Maintain volunteer records and compliance.
Coordinate Working With Children Checks, port inductions, First Aid and other required training.
Develop volunteer rosters where applicable.
6. Financial Administration
Assist with day-to-day financial administration.
Process invoices and expenses.
Support budgeting and financial reporting.
Maintain accurate records using Xero or equivalent systems.
7. Stakeholder Engagement
Develop productive relationships with:
Flinders Ports
Shipping agents
Maritime unions
AMSA
Australian Border Force
Port Welfare Committees
Local churches
Community organisations
Government agencies
Represent Mission to Seafarers at meetings and forums as required.

Attend:
South Australian committee meetings.
National Mission to Seafarers conferences.
Volunteer training events.
Industry meetings and conferences.
Ship visits across South Australian ports.
Other duties as directed by the Regional Director.

Employment Conditions
The position is offered as a job-share arrangement, with two Port Welfare Officers working collaboratively to provide consistent coverage across South Australia.
The combined role is funded at 5Days per week, with flexibility to increase hours through project funding or centre development initiatives.
Regular travel throughout South Australia is an essential component of the role, with a Mission vehicle available where appropriate.
Comprehensive on-the-job training will be provided.
The role would suit someone with several years of workplace experience who enjoys working with people, is comfortable travelling, and wants to make a meaningful contribution to the wellbeing of international seafarers visiting South Australian ports.

Employer: EDS Support Australia Pty Ltd
Position: Speech Pathologist
Employment Type: Full-Time (Part-Time may be considered)
Location: Mareeba, Far North Queensland, with regular travel throughout Cairns, Tablelands, Cape York and surrounding regional, remote and very remote communities.
Salary: $95,000 – $125,000 per annum + Superannuation + Travel Allowance (where applicable)
Reports To: Clinical Manager / Director
________________________________________
About EDS Support Australia Pty Ltd
EDS Support Australia Pty Ltd is a community-based allied health and disability service provider delivering high-quality services throughout Far North Queensland. We support children, adolescents and adults through NDIS-funded and community-based programs, focusing on early intervention, capacity building, communication, independence and participation.
We are committed to delivering culturally safe, person-centred and evidence-based services across metropolitan, regional, remote and very remote communities.
________________________________________
Position Summary
The Speech Pathologist will provide comprehensive assessment, diagnosis, intervention and ongoing therapy services for children with developmental delays, communication disorders, autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability, neurological conditions and other complex needs.
The role primarily supports children funded through the NDIS and community programs while working collaboratively with families, schools, childcare centres, healthcare providers and multidisciplinary teams.
This position requires extensive community outreach and travel throughout Far North Queensland, including remote and very remote communities.
________________________________________
Key Responsibilities
The Speech Pathologist will:
•	Conduct comprehensive speech, language, communication, literacy and swallowing assessments.
•	Assess children presenting with developmental delays and complex communication needs.
•	Complete functional assessments that support NDIS access and plan reviews.
•	Develop evidence-based therapy plans aligned with participant goals.
•	Deliver individual and group therapy sessions.
•	Provide early childhood intervention services.
•	Prepare high-quality clinical reports, assessment reports, progress reports and therapy recommendations.
•	Develop communication strategies for home, school and community environments.
•	Prescribe and implement Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) systems where appropriate.
•	Educate parents, carers, teachers and support workers.
•	Participate in multidisciplinary case conferences.
•	Liaise with paediatricians, GPs, psychologists, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, educators and support coordinators.
•	Maintain accurate documentation consistent with NDIS Practice Standards.
•	Provide outreach services across regional, remote and very remote communities.
•	Deliver services via clinic, home visits, schools, childcare centres, community settings and telehealth where appropriate.
•	Participate in quality improvement activities and professional development.
________________________________________
Essential Selection Criteria
Applicants must possess:
Qualifications
•	Bachelor or Master's Degree in Speech Pathology.
•	Eligibility for Certified Practising Speech Pathologist (CPSP) status with Speech Pathology Australia.
Experience
•	Minimum two (2) years' clinical experience (desirable).
•	Experience assessing and treating children with communication disorders.
•	Experience working within the NDIS.
•	Experience working in community-based allied health services.
•	Demonstrated experience completing functional assessments and clinical reports.
•	Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.
Skills
•	Excellent assessment and clinical reasoning skills.
•	Strong report writing ability.
•	Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
•	Ability to work independently.
•	Effective time management.
•	Strong organisational skills.
•	Ability to manage a varied caseload.
•	High level of cultural awareness.
•	Commitment to evidence-based practice.
Mandatory Requirements
•	AHPRA Registration – Speech Pathologist
•	Current Australian Driver Licence (Essential).
•	Willingness to travel regularly throughout Far North Queensland.
•	Ability to work in regional, remote and very remote communities.
•	Current NDIS Worker Screening Clearance.
•	Current Queensland Blue Card (Working with Children Check).
•	Current National Police Check.
•	Current First Aid and CPR Certificate.
•	COVID-19 and other vaccinations as required by funding bodies or host organisations.
•	Australian working rights or eligibility for employer-sponsored visa.
________________________________________
Desirable
•	Experience working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities.
•	Rural and remote healthcare experience.
•	Experience with AAC systems.
•	Knowledge of Positive Behaviour Support.
•	Experience delivering telehealth services.
•	Experience with paediatric feeding and swallowing disorders.
•	Knowledge of sensory communication approaches.
________________________________________
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
The successful Speech Pathologist will:
•	Meet agreed billable clinical targets.
•	Complete assessments within organisational timeframes.
•	Maintain high-quality clinical documentation.
•	Achieve participant goal outcomes.
•	Maintain participant satisfaction.
•	Participate in clinical supervision.
•	Maintain professional development requirements.
•	Comply with NDIS Practice Standards and organisational policies.
•	Demonstrate effective collaboration with multidisciplinary teams.
________________________________________
Compliance Requirements
The successful applicant must comply with:
•	NDIS Practice Standards.
•	NDIS Code of Conduct.
•	Child Safe Standards.
•	Privacy legislation.
•	Workplace Health and Safety requirements.
•	Infection prevention and control procedures.
•	Mandatory reporting obligations.
•	Clinical governance framework.
•	Continuous Quality Improvement activities.
________________________________________
Benefits
EDS Support Australia Pty Ltd offers:
•	Competitive salary package.
•	Superannuation.
•	Professional development allowance.
•	Paid professional development leave.
•	Clinical supervision and mentoring.
•	Flexible work arrangements.
•	Travel reimbursement.
•	Laptop and mobile phone.
•	Career progression opportunities.
•	Opportunity to work within a multidisciplinary allied health team.
•	Employer-sponsored visa opportunities for suitable overseas applicants who meet Australian migration and professional registration requirements.
________________________________________
Employer-Sponsored Visa Eligibility (where applicable)

•	Meet Australian migration requirements for employer sponsorship.
•	Hold recognised Speech Pathology qualifications – AHPRA Registration
•	Meet English language requirements.
•	Are eligible for Certified Practising Speech Pathologist (CPSP) status with Speech Pathology Australia.
•	Meet all pre-employment screening requirements.
________________________________________
Our Commitment
EDS Support Australia Pty Ltd is committed to safeguarding children and vulnerable people. We value diversity and encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, culturally and linguistically diverse communities, and professionals committed to improving health outcomes across regional, remote and very remote Australia.
